name: status-hud
description: Pixel-style status HUD: every session's context fill, host load, memory, disks, GPU, the Windows commit limit and mode chips, as a band above the prompt or a side pane.

variant.title: Variant
variant.description: band draws the 10-row band above the prompt, pane opens the side pane, off draws nothing (sessions still report).

contextAmberMark.title: Context amber mark (tokens)
contextAmberMark.description: A session at or above this many context tokens turns amber.

contextReportMark.title: Context report mark (tokens)
contextReportMark.description: At or above this the session turns red, and flashes red when it crosses.

flashSeconds.title: Report flash seconds
flashSeconds.description: How long a session flashes red after crossing the report mark. 0 disables the flash.

commitWarnPct.title: Windows commit warn %
commitWarnPct.description: Amber at this percent of the Windows commit limit, red at commitCritPct.

commitCritPct.title: Windows commit critical %
commitCritPct.description: Red at this percent of the Windows commit limit.

commitCmd.title: Commit-limit command
commitCmd.description: Shell command that prints '<limitKB> <freeKB>' (Windows TotalVirtualMemorySize and FreeVirtualMemory). Empty disables the warning. Slow (about a second), so it runs at most every commitSeconds.

commitSeconds.title: Commit check seconds
commitSeconds.description: Minimum seconds between Windows commit readings.

mounts.title: Disk mounts
mounts.description: Comma-separated mount points to show, e.g. /,/data.

showForNames.title: Show in sessions
showForNames.description: Comma-separated session names that draw the HUD, e.g. Orca,Vali (kit-init sets it to your seat). Exact and case-sensitive. Empty shows it in every session. Every session still writes its heartbeat either way.

dotMode.title: Session dot
dotMode.description: What each session row's dot shows: account (blue = Claude account 1, purple = account 2) or project (the color of the session's terminal tab when its launcher recorded one, else its project's color), so several projects' teams are told apart.

hideItems.title: Hidden items
hideItems.description: Comma-separated ids of items to switch off, e.g. history,context-key (README: Items). The setup page (scripts/hud-guide.sh open in the kit) picks them on a picture.

kitRuntimeDir.title: Kit runtime dir
kitRuntimeDir.description: Where the kit's launcher records each project's tab color (the tab-colors file), read for project dots. A missing file is fine.

statusDir.title: Status directory
statusDir.description: Shared directory for heartbeats and host.json. Empty means ~/.claude-status-hud.

sessionName.title: Session name
sessionName.description: Overrides the name detected from the claude command line (--name).

refreshSeconds.title: Refresh seconds
refreshSeconds.description: Seconds between heartbeat writes and redraws.

staleSeconds.title: Stale seconds
staleSeconds.description: A session whose heartbeat is older than this is shown as gone and then dropped.

cpuRedLoad.title: CPU red load
cpuRedLoad.description: 1-minute load average at which the CPU bar turns red. 0 means 90% of the thread count.

quietModeFlagFile.title: Quiet mode flag file
quietModeFlagFile.description: If set, this file existing means quiet mode is on (cheap check). The default is the orchestration kit's flag (scripts/quiet-mode.sh writes it; a leading ~ means your home). Empty uses quietModeStatusCmd.

quietModeStatusCmd.title: Quiet mode status command
quietModeStatusCmd.description: Shell command whose exit code 0 means quiet mode is on. Empty with no flag file hides the quiet mode chip.

quietModeOnCmd.title: Quiet mode on command
quietModeOnCmd.description: Shell command run when the Quiet Mode chip switches it on. Runs in the session's directory, so the default finds the kit's scripts/quiet-mode.sh in your repo.

quietModeOffCmd.title: Quiet mode off command
quietModeOffCmd.description: Shell command run when the Quiet Mode chip switches it off.

quietModeRequiresFile.title: Quiet mode script (chip visibility)
quietModeRequiresFile.description: The chip is shown only when this file exists in the session's directory (or quiet mode is already on), because the on/off commands need it. A relative path resolves against the session directory. Empty always shows the chip.
